content.text: {"intent_summary":{"statement":"MPOP is Serindit Pay's Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform. It accepts merchant payment requests, routes each one to an acquirer, e-wallet provider or bank-transfer rail, and accounts for every resulting money movement until the money is settled and paid out to the merchant. It replaces five per-market integration stacks with one merchant API across five Southeast Asian markets. It covers rule-based routing with cascading, idempotency, a PCI-scoped tokenising vault, a synchronous fraud hook, a double-entry ledger, daily three-way reconciliation, payouts, signed webhooks and a merchant admin plane, sized for about 15,000 merchants and a peak of 2,000 payment-creation TPS by 2027. Disputes, KYB, 3DS server internals, lending/BNPL and checkout UIs are out of scope.","objectives":[{"ref":null,"text":"Replace five per-market integration stacks that share no routing or ledger and reconcile by spreadsheet with one governed platform."},{"ref":null,"text":"Provide one versioned merchant API across five markets (SG, MY, ID, TH, PH) for cards, e-wallets and bank transfers."},{"ref":null,"text":"Support about 15,000 active merchants, 10.5M attempts per day and a peak of 2,000 create-payment TPS (2027 target)."},{"ref":"P1","text":"One payment, one truth: the payment record and the ledger are the source of truth; provider responses are only inputs."},{"ref":"P2","text":"Card data stays in the Vault: PAN and SAD never leave the Vault boundary except over the Card Adapter's acquirer connection; all other services handle tokens only."},{"ref":"P3","text":"Idempotency is scoped to (merchant, key) for every mutating call."},{"ref":"P4","text":"Money is integers: amounts are integer minor units with an ISO 4217 code; no floating point."},{"ref":"P5","text":"The ledger is append-only; corrections are new reversing or adjusting journals."},{"ref":"P6","text":"Adapters absorb provider differences; the core never branches on provider identity."},{"ref":"P7","text":"At-least-once delivery with exactly-once effect through consumer deduplication on stable identifiers."},{"ref":"P8","text":"Fail closed on security; degrade gracefully to documented defaults on optional enrichment (fraud signals, BIN metadata)."},{"ref":"P9","text":"Least privilege and separation of duties; money-moving permissions are separated from configuration permissions."},{"ref":"P10","text":"Everything is auditable: every mutation, routing decision and admin action can be reconstructed."}],"constraints":[{"ref":"NFR-5","text":"Must be assessed as a PCI DSS v4.0 Level 1 service provider, with the CDE limited to the components in Section 12.2."},{"ref":"NFR-6","text":"Sensitive authentication data must be handled per PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2."},{"ref":"NFR-7","text":"Personal data must be processed under SG PDPA 2012, MY PDPA 2010, ID Law 27/2022, TH PDPA 2019 and PH DPA 2012."},{"ref":"FR-7","text":"Card reattempts must never occur where card scheme rules prohibit them."},{"ref":null,"text":"Principles P1-P10 override any later section that appears to conflict with them."},{"ref":null,"text":"All primary data stores are in AWS ap-southeast-1. The ap-southeast-3 Aurora secondary is for disaster recovery only."},{"ref":null,"text":"Out of scope: dispute case management (disputes are ledger events only), merchant onboarding/KYB (Merchant Risk platform), 3DS server internals (third party), lending/BNPL/instalments, and checkout UIs/SDKs."},{"ref":null,"text":"ACQ-PH1 retires API v2 in Q3 2027."},{"ref":null,"text":"Retention: payment and attempt records 7 years; idempotency records 24 hours; webhook events 30 days; raw settlement files 7 years; audit records 5 years."},{"ref":null,"text":"Rollout: the first cohort (Singapore, cards and PayNow) goes live after Phase 7; other markets follow at four-week intervals."}],"key_assumptions":[{"ref":null,"text":"The largest merchant (M-0001) accounts for about 45% of peak traffic (about 900 TPS). Each request uses two DynamoDB writes, staying within a stated 10,000 WCU per-partition ceiling."},{"ref":null,"text":"Fewer than 1% of card payments cascade, so cascading does not affect the p99 latency budget. Retryable outcomes were 3.8% in the 2025 baseline."},{"ref":null,"text":"The acquirer round trip p99 is 1,100 ms (2025 production, slowest acquirer), and HSM detokenise takes 20 ms per a vendor benchmark."},{"ref":null,"text":"An Aurora spike on db.r7g.8xlarge sustained 2,600 TPS of the full write mix. Production uses db.r7g.12xlarge for headroom."},{"ref":null,"text":"A single CloudHSM in one AZ is sufficient at launch. A second HSM will be added when sustained card volume exceeds 1,500 TPS."},{"ref":null,"text":"The document states that PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 permit encrypted SAD/CVC retention until settlement."},{"ref":null,"text":"FRV-1 requires the full card number for its consortium velocity graph, and the Fraud Hook obtains it via detokenise."},{"ref":null,"text":"Network tokens (VTS/MDES) are available from launch as the primary card-on-file credential."},{"ref":null,"text":"The reconciliation matcher takes 45 minutes and report generation 15 minutes at 2025 volume; the matcher starts only after all files are received."},{"ref":null,"text":"Cascading recovered about 31% of retryable outcomes in a three-month ACQ-SG1 → ACQ-SG2 pilot."},{"ref":null,"text":"The first merchant cohort does not need the Admin API schemas or the dispute module (it uses the portal; Finance Operations handles disputes
